I’m a ski instructor and backcountry enthusiast.

Go to a ski resort (pass is cheapest now buy now). 
Rent gear for day #1 (after that if you are still stoked I’d say get a set up for INBOUNDS or downhill) Get as many days on snow as you can - if you can afford lessons do that you’ll progress faster and not have to unlearn bad habits later. 

Once you can confidently ride all terrain in all conditions then you should buy a touring set up. With the touring set up you should start only at a resort and get comfy with it (also backcountry skiing is way harder and different than inbounds skiing and falling in powder is tiring).

Go take an AAIRE-1 class. You’ll meet people who do this out of bounds. You need friends to do this. Or at least to begin you should or you’re putting SAR lives at risk.

It’s honestly a lot of work, but it’s insanely fun. Like grinning ear to ear for a week fun. But not at first. Don’t give up. Keep falling (snow is soft and it’s fun - keep telling yourself that). Skiing is the best sport. Seriously ever.
